items.stem: A 5-Whys analysis ends at 'the technician did not grease the bearing'. Why is this usually an inadequate root cause?

options.text: It names a human action but not the system reason that allowed it
options.rationale: Correct: effective RCA continues to the systemic cause, e.g. a missing or unclear PM task, so the fix prevents recurrence.

options.text: Human error can never be a contributing factor
options.rationale: Human error can contribute, but it is rarely the deepest actionable cause.

options.text: 5-Whys should always stop at exactly five whys
options.rationale: The number is a guide; you continue until a controllable systemic cause is found.

options.text: Bearings do not fail from lack of grease
options.rationale: Lubrication loss is a valid physical mechanism; the issue is stopping the analysis too early.

items.explanation: Correct: effective RCA continues to the systemic cause, e.g. a missing or unclear PM task, so the fix prevents recurrence.

items.stem: Immediately after a failure, which TWO actions best preserve evidence for RCA? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Photograph and tag the failed parts before cleaning them
options.rationale: Correct: physical evidence must be captured in its as-found state.

options.text: Record operator accounts and recent operating data
options.rationale: Correct: people and paper/data are part of the evidence and are quickly lost.

options.text: Clean and reinstall the failed component to restore service fast
options.rationale: Cleaning destroys physical evidence needed to find the mechanism.

options.text: Decide the likely cause first, then collect only supporting data
options.rationale: That invites confirmation bias and ignores disconfirming evidence.

items.explanation: Correct: physical evidence must be captured in its as-found state.

items.stem: Using the hierarchy of controls, which corrective action is most likely to prevent recurrence of an over-torqued bolted joint?

options.text: Design the joint so the correct torque is built in or hard to get wrong
options.rationale: Correct: elimination/engineering controls outrank reminders and training in reliability.

options.text: Add a reminder note on the work order
options.rationale: Reminders are weak administrative controls that rely on memory.

options.text: Retrain the technician who made the error
options.rationale: Training alone is a weak control and fades over time.

options.text: Ask the team to be more careful
options.rationale: Exhortation is the weakest control and rarely prevents recurrence.

items.explanation: Correct: elimination/engineering controls outrank reminders and training in reliability.
